what_worked: Power-law concentration theme is genuine and well-illustrated across multiple slides with consistent design.
fix_next: Fix the false 'no founding dates' claim, correct the .ai-leads-revenue subtitle that contradicts your own chart, and add missingness/limitations.
verdict: Clean template tour of the data with several factual errors and missing key analyses.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: claims 'dataset has no founding dates' — false, 984 founded-year/revenue pairs exist. Slide 7: subtitle says '.ai leads on both domain authority and revenue per company' but own chart shows .com ($391K) > .ai ($364K). Slide 7: .com count shown as 317 vs reference 312.

evidence.insight: Power-law concentration (slides 2, 10) and B2B vs B2C comparison (slide 9) are useful but surface-level. No provider, anonymity, or founded-year analysis attempted. Most slides describe rather than synthesize.
evidence.narrative: Logical arc from overview → categories → momentum → reach → leaderboard → domains → audience → power law. Closing slide attempts synthesis with three takeaways. Reads as a data tour rather than a story driven by a central question.
evidence.framing: Scope stated (1,000 startups) but no audience defined, no decision context, no limitations discussed. Missingness (24-29% across key fields) never acknowledged. False claim about no founding dates undermines credibility.
evidence.accuracy: Three confirmed errors: false 'no founding dates' claim contradicts 984 usable pairs; .ai revenue-per-company claim contradicted by own chart; .com count 317 vs 312. Category totals and company counts use an all-time column not in the frozen reference, making most revenue figures unverifiable.
evidence.visual: Consistent color palette, clean card layout, good whitespace, legible data labels on charts. Grouped bar chart (slide 4) well-annotated. Template-driven repetition (card after card) reduces visual variety. No in-chart annotations highlighting key comparisons.
evidence.ai_slop: Clearly AI-generated template (likely Gamma). 'Prepared as a data narrative · Neutral, factual tone' is boilerplate. Visual sameness across slides. Content is substantive enough to avoid pure slop but lacks originality in presentation.

change_reason: Reduced framing from 5.0 to 4.5 for false founding-dates claim and zero limitations discussion. Reduced factual error count from 8 to 3 confirmed errors — preliminary overcounted by treating unverifiable all-time figures as errors. Other scores held steady after independent review.
